headline: Amended and approved May 13 minutes, discussed pool construction, park analysis, and future pool fees.
summary: The commission amended and approved the May 13, 2026 minutes to add a note about Kenny Michaels joining the Connecticut Parks and Recreation Association board. Staff gave updates on pool construction, timed for fall 2026 completion and a 2027 opening, and on a park analysis that could lead to a town parks master plan. The commission discussed possible pool program fees and resident-only access for the first year, and agreed to bring more ideas to the next meeting. Members also discussed a past basketball league incident, an unsent letter about bow hunting, and sprinkler watering issues at Vets Field.
decisions: Amended the May 13, 2026 minutes to include discussion of Kenny Michaels' election to the Connecticut Parks and Recreation Association Board of Directors; unanimously approved.
Approved the May 13, 2026 minutes as amended; unanimously approved.
plain_text:
Wallingford Parks & Recreation Commission 
Special Meeting Agenda 
Wallingford Parks & Recreation Building 
6 Fairfield Blvd. Wallingford, CT 06492   
September 2, 2026 @ 5:30 P .M. 
Room 4 
Meeting was called to order at 5:39pm. 
1. Pledge of Allegiance 
2. Roll Call 
- Commissioners in Attendance: Don Crouch, Steve Rossacci, Dave Anderson, 
Lori Cooke Marra 
- Recreation Staff in Attendance: Kenny Michaels and Shawn Keogh 
3. Public Comments (10 minutes total time) 
- None  
4. Approval of Minutes May 13, 2026 
 - Motion made by Dave Anderson to amend the May 13th minutes to to include the 
discussion that Kenny Michaels was elected to the Board of Directors for the Connecticut 
Parks and Recreation Association. Second by Lori Cooke-Marra. Unanimously approved. 
 - Motion made by Steve Rossacci to approve the May 13th minutes as amended. 
Second by Lori Cooke-Marra. Unanimously approved. 
5. Reports 
a. Director 
- Director Report attached. Kenny reviewed his report.  
b. Project Updates 
i. Community Pool Park 
 -Pool construction is ongoing.  Conduits are being run for cameras to be 
installed in the future. Kenny is meeting with IT to determine the best method for 
cameras. Project is estimated to be completed in the fall of 2026 and ready to be 
opened in 2027. 
ii. Park Analysis 
- Kenny discussed several parks in town and how this can start the 
discussion on a master plan for the town parks. Analysis is attached.  
c. Chairman 
-none 
6. Old Business
- Steve Rossacci asked about the Summer Basketball League that is run by the Boys 
& Girls Club after an incident that occurred this past summer. The players involved in the 
incident were removed from the league and the league was allowed to continue as normal. 
-Dave asked about the letter to the mayor regarding bow hunting that was discussed 
at the February meeting. It was discussed at past meetings, but the letter was not sent by 
the commission. Don will send a letter with the corresponding minutes from the February 
meeting.  
7. New Business 
a. Discussion: Community Pool Program Fees 
- Kenny reviewed the original plan of pool passes from the Pool Committee in 2019 
and fees that are charged in surrounding towns. The commission discussed some 
possibilities of future pool passes. The commission would like to see residents only for at 
least the first year of the pool. The splash pad will be open to the public. Kenny has also 
been working on the possibility of soliciting sponsorships to offset the costs of some of the 
features at the pool. The commission will brainstorm and bring back their thoughts on fees 
to the next meeting. 
8. Commission Around Town 
a. Comments/Concerns 
- Dave Anderson wanted to give props to Bob Kilpatrick and Max Robbins on the Fall 
2026 brochure. He really enjoys the way the brochure looks and thinks it’s a great product.  
-Lori asked about the watering at Vets Field. She noticed the sprinklers were on 
during rain, there are no sensors to shut the sprinklers off. DPW manually shuts them off 
when they can when it is raining.  
9. Adjournment 
-Motion made to adjourn by Lori Cooke-Marra. Second by Dave Anderson. All in favor  
Meeting adjourned at 7:39pm.  
 
Respectfully submitted,  
Shawn Keogh 
Recreation Superintendent
